Stiff-Man Syndrome with GAD-Like 
Immunoreactivity: Response of a Patient to 
Plasmapheresis and Immunosuppression 
H.R. Brashear and Lawrence H. Phillips 11, Charlottesville, VA 
Objective. To study immunological, clinical and electrophysio- 
logical responses to treatment of stiff-man syndrome. 
Background. Some patients with a diagnosis of stiff-man syn- 
drome have circulating autoantibodies with GAD-like 
immunoreactivity (GAD-LIR). We report our second patient with 
stiff-man syndrome, high titers of serum GAD-LIR and typical 
EMG findings who responded to treatment. 
Methods. Indirect immunofluorescence assays, clinical 
assessments, and exteroceptive reflex measurements were car- 
ried out before, during and after plasmapheresis and immuno- 
suppression with corticosteroids. 
Results. Plasmapheresis and immunosuppression resulted in 
decreased titers of GAD-LIR, marked improvement in rigidity 
and spasms, and reduced amplitude of exteroceptive reflexes. 
Although clinical and electrophysiological improvement persist- 
ed on steroids, antibody titers returned to previous levels. 
Unlike our previously reported patient (Neurology 
1992;41:1588), this woman had detectable antibody in the CSF 
and developed seizures in late life. 
Conclusions. These results further support the use of serum 
GAD-LIR and exteroceptive reflexes as markers for stiff-man 
syndrome. Our findings also suggest that serum GAD-LIR may 
identify a subset of patients responsive to treatment, that corti- 
costeroids may be efficacious even with increasing titers, and 
that CSF GAD-LIR is a risk factor for seizures.
